messages.subject: Optimizing Error
parts:
I am analyzing a big data set with a lot of missing values, and a lot of parameters. MCMC takes almost unmanageably long to fit the data. Stan's optimizers seem to work great at finding a reasonable MAP estimate. I'd like to get some kind of confidence intervals on the MAP, however, and this seems to be impossible.

R claims it would need more than 200 gigs of ram to calculate the Hessian matrix (this is mostly due the large number of missing data parameters). Is there a way of getting some kind of quadratic approximation of the likelihood function in the neighborhood of the MAP for a smaller sub-set of regression parameters that I care about?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Optimizing Error (scalability of Hessian at mode)
parts:
A 200GB Hessian would entail something north of 150K params?
We should probably work on saving half the space in the Hessian
storage.

There's nothing built-in to do Hessians on only some params
that I know of.

The best you could do is compute it yourself by taking
finite differences based on the gradients. That's pretty
much what's going on under the hood at the moment anyway
in RStan.

We will be replacing the finite-diffs approach with one
based on 2nd order autodiff that should be more efficient.

- Bob
